$comment: The R2 configuration this codebase DEPENDS ON, per environment.
Read by 95-verify-r2.sh (compares it to the live account, read-only) and by
backend/test/infra/r2_manifest_test.dart (compares it to the code, offline).
Those two directions are the point: the test catches a manifest that has
drifted from what the backend actually does, and the script catches an
account that has drifted from the manifest. Neither alone is enough.
PROPERTIES, NOT SNAPSHOTS. Everything here is a floor — 'the rule must exist',
'these methods must be allowed' — never an exact copy of the live config.
Production and staging already differ cosmetically (production allows any
header and no HEAD; staging allows content-type, HEAD, and exposes etag), and
a checker that failed on that would be turned off within a month.
Rules are matched by PREFIX AND ACTION, never by name: production's pending
rule is called expire-unclaimed-uploads and staging's expire-pending-uploads,
because production was configured by hand before the staging script existed.
A name-matched check would report the production rule as missing.

production.$corsComment: www.myweli.com is also allowed live; only the apex is required.

staging.$corsComment: Staging has no deployed web origin yet — infra-staging.md step 5. When one exists, add it here FIRST and the checker will tell you the bucket has not caught up.

lifecycle.$comment: Required on EVERY bucket in both environments. The promotion design in backend-upload-orphans.md rests entirely on this rule: an object under this prefix has never been claimed, so expiring it cannot delete anything a user still needs. Without it, `pending/` grows forever and the T61 size cap never applies to an unclaimed upload.

cors.$comment: Public bucket only — the private KYC and deposit buckets are never read by a browser. The methods are what a presigned-PUT upload from the web app performs; the content-type header is what the presign SIGNS, so a bucket that strips it turns every browser upload into a 403 from storage.
